display.name: Hub · Pulse
display.description: Production at a glance: polling, traffic, queues and Supabase archival. Metrics include unsampled work; freshness distinguishes quiet from offline.

display.name: Telemetry age
display.description: Seconds since the newest production metric. With 60s collection: amber after 90s, red after 180s; empty means no observation in the selected window.

spec.query: SELECT EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - MAX(recorded_timestamp))) AS seconds FROM metrics WHERE service_name = 'msu-hub-bot' AND deployment_environment = 'production'

display.name: Since last good poll
display.description: Latest reported seconds since a successful Telegram poll. Read alongside telemetry age.

spec.query: SELECT scalar_value AS seconds FROM metrics WHERE service_name = 'msu-hub-bot' AND deployment_environment = 'production' AND metric_name = 'bot.poll.age' ORDER BY recorded_timestamp DESC LIMIT 1

display.name: Handler runs
display.description: Completed non-ignored handlers during the selected interval, from unsampled counters. Totals separate process/counter epochs and include initial values only for epochs starting within the selected window.

spec.query:
WITH streams AS (
    SELECT
        service_version, service_instance_id, process_pid,
        CASE WHEN aggregation_temporality = 'cumulative' THEN start_timestamp END AS counter_epoch,
        aggregation_temporality,
        attributes->>'boundary' AS boundary,
        attributes->>'operation' AS operation,
        attributes->>'outcome' AS outcome,
        attributes->>'provider' AS provider,
        attributes->>'backend' AS backend,
        attributes->>'update.kind' AS update_kind,
        metric_increase(value, recorded_timestamp)
            + CASE WHEN aggregation_temporality = 'cumulative'
                AND MIN(start_timestamp) >= CAST($__from_iso_string AS TIMESTAMPTZ)
                AND MIN(start_timestamp) <= CAST($__to_iso_string AS TIMESTAMPTZ)
                THEN COALESCE(MIN(scalar_value), 0) ELSE 0 END AS n
    FROM metrics
    WHERE service_name = 'msu-hub-bot' AND deployment_environment = 'production'
      AND metric_name = 'bot.operations' AND attributes->>'boundary' = 'bot.handler' AND attributes->>'outcome' <> 'ignored'
    GROUP BY service_version, service_instance_id, process_pid, counter_epoch, aggregation_temporality, boundary, operation, outcome, provider, backend, update_kind
)
SELECT SUM(n) AS runs FROM streams

display.name: Handler failures
display.description: Unavailable, timeout or unexpected handler outcomes in this interval, from unsampled counters. Totals separate process/counter epochs and include initial values only for epochs starting within the selected window.

spec.query:
WITH streams AS (
    SELECT
        service_version, service_instance_id, process_pid,
        CASE WHEN aggregation_temporality = 'cumulative' THEN start_timestamp END AS counter_epoch,
        aggregation_temporality,
        attributes->>'boundary' AS boundary,
        attributes->>'operation' AS operation,
        attributes->>'outcome' AS outcome,
        attributes->>'provider' AS provider,
        attributes->>'backend' AS backend,
        attributes->>'update.kind' AS update_kind,
        metric_increase(value, recorded_timestamp)
            + CASE WHEN aggregation_temporality = 'cumulative'
                AND MIN(start_timestamp) >= CAST($__from_iso_string AS TIMESTAMPTZ)
                AND MIN(start_timestamp) <= CAST($__to_iso_string AS TIMESTAMPTZ)
                THEN COALESCE(MIN(scalar_value), 0) ELSE 0 END AS n
    FROM metrics
    WHERE service_name = 'msu-hub-bot' AND deployment_environment = 'production'
      AND metric_name = 'bot.operations' AND attributes->>'boundary' = 'bot.handler' AND attributes->>'outcome' <> 'ignored'
    GROUP BY service_version, service_instance_id, process_pid, counter_epoch, aggregation_temporality, boundary, operation, outcome, provider, backend, update_kind
)
SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN outcome IN ('unavailable', 'timeout', 'unexpected') THEN n ELSE 0 END) AS failures FROM streams

display.name: Latest telemetry
display.description: Latest observed gauges, their age and deployment. A stale sample or missing series needs attention.

spec.query:
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT recorded_timestamp, service_version, metric_name, scalar_value,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY metric_name ORDER BY recorded_timestamp DESC) AS position
    FROM metrics
    WHERE service_name = 'msu-hub-bot' AND deployment_environment = 'production'
      AND metric_name IN ('bot.poll.age', 'bot.updates.active', 'bot.jobs.active', 'bot.workers.active', 'bot.workers.queued')
)
SELECT metric_name AS signal, scalar_value AS last_value, recorded_timestamp AS sampled_at,
       EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (now() - recorded_timestamp)) AS sample_age_seconds, service_version AS release
FROM latest WHERE position = 1 ORDER BY signal

display.name: Polling age
display.description: Seconds since a successful Telegram poll, using the peak per bucket. Gaps mean telemetry was not received.

spec.query:
SELECT time_bucket($resolution, recorded_timestamp) AS x,
       MAX(scalar_value) AS seconds_since_success
FROM metrics
WHERE service_name = 'msu-hub-bot' AND deployment_environment = 'production' AND metric_name = 'bot.poll.age'
GROUP BY x ORDER BY x

display.name: Polling outcomes
display.description: Completed Telegram polling attempts per minute. Successful empty polls count too.

spec.query:
WITH streams AS (
    SELECT
        time_bucket($resolution, recorded_timestamp) AS x,
        service_version, service_instance_id, process_pid,
        CASE WHEN aggregation_temporality = 'cumulative' THEN start_timestamp END AS counter_epoch,
        aggregation_temporality,
        attributes->>'boundary' AS boundary,
        attributes->>'operation' AS operation,
        attributes->>'outcome' AS outcome,
        attributes->>'provider' AS provider,
        attributes->>'backend' AS backend,
        attributes->>'update.kind' AS update_kind,
        metric_rate(value, recorded_timestamp) AS n
    FROM metrics
    WHERE service_name = 'msu-hub-bot' AND deployment_environment = 'production'
      AND metric_name = 'bot.poll.requests'
    GROUP BY x, service_version, service_instance_id, process_pid, counter_epoch, aggregation_temporality, boundary, operation, outcome, provider, backend, update_kind
)
SELECT x, outcome, 60 * SUM(n) AS requests_per_minute
FROM streams GROUP BY x, outcome ORDER BY x, outcome

display.name: Update outcomes
display.description: Completed update dispatches per minute, including ignored messages. One result per update.

spec.query:
WITH streams AS (
    SELECT
        time_bucket($resolution, recorded_timestamp) AS x,
        service_version, service_instance_id, process_pid,
        CASE WHEN aggregation_temporality = 'cumulative' THEN start_timestamp END AS counter_epoch,
        aggregation_temporality,
        attributes->>'boundary' AS boundary,
        attributes->>'operation' AS operation,
        attributes->>'outcome' AS outcome,
        attributes->>'provider' AS provider,
        attributes->>'backend' AS backend,
        attributes->>'update.kind' AS update_kind,
        metric_rate(value, recorded_timestamp) AS n
    FROM metrics
    WHERE service_name = 'msu-hub-bot' AND deployment_environment = 'production'
      AND metric_name = 'bot.operations' AND attributes->>'boundary' = 'bot.dispatch' AND attributes->>'operation' = 'dispatch'
    GROUP BY x, service_version, service_instance_id, process_pid, counter_epoch, aggregation_temporality, boundary, operation, outcome, provider, backend, update_kind
)
SELECT x, outcome, 60 * SUM(n) AS updates_per_minute
FROM streams GROUP BY x, outcome ORDER BY x, outcome

display.name: Active work
display.description: Peak updates, jobs, active workers and queued work. Useful for spotting a backlog.

spec.query:
SELECT time_bucket($resolution, recorded_timestamp) AS x, metric_name AS work,
       MAX(scalar_value) AS peak_active
FROM metrics
WHERE service_name = 'msu-hub-bot' AND deployment_environment = 'production'
  AND metric_name IN ('bot.updates.active', 'bot.jobs.active', 'bot.workers.active', 'bot.workers.queued')
GROUP BY x, work ORDER BY x, work

display.name: Update archival
display.description: Supabase archive operations per minute, separated by outcome.

spec.query:
WITH streams AS (
    SELECT
        time_bucket($resolution, recorded_timestamp) AS x,
        service_version, service_instance_id, process_pid,
        CASE WHEN aggregation_temporality = 'cumulative' THEN start_timestamp END AS counter_epoch,
        aggregation_temporality,
        attributes->>'boundary' AS boundary,
        attributes->>'operation' AS operation,
        attributes->>'outcome' AS outcome,
        attributes->>'provider' AS provider,
        attributes->>'backend' AS backend,
        attributes->>'update.kind' AS update_kind,
        metric_rate(value, recorded_timestamp) AS n
    FROM metrics
    WHERE service_name = 'msu-hub-bot' AND deployment_environment = 'production'
      AND metric_name = 'bot.operations' AND attributes->>'boundary' = 'storage.operation' AND attributes->>'operation' = 'archive.write'
    GROUP BY x, service_version, service_instance_id, process_pid, counter_epoch, aggregation_temporality, boundary, operation, outcome, provider, backend, update_kind
)
SELECT x, outcome, 60 * SUM(n) AS archive_writes_per_minute
FROM streams GROUP BY x, outcome ORDER BY x, outcome

display.name: Telemetry queue losses
display.description: Queue and emission drops during the selected interval. Read alongside telemetry freshness. Totals separate process/counter epochs and include initial values only for epochs starting within the selected window.

spec.query:
WITH streams AS (
    SELECT metric_name, service_version, service_instance_id, process_pid,
        CASE WHEN aggregation_temporality = 'cumulative' THEN start_timestamp END AS counter_epoch,
        aggregation_temporality,
           metric_increase(value, recorded_timestamp)
            + CASE WHEN aggregation_temporality = 'cumulative'
                AND MIN(start_timestamp) >= CAST($__from_iso_string AS TIMESTAMPTZ)
                AND MIN(start_timestamp) <= CAST($__to_iso_string AS TIMESTAMPTZ)
                THEN COALESCE(MIN(scalar_value), 0) ELSE 0 END AS dropped
    FROM metrics
    WHERE service_name = 'msu-hub-bot' AND deployment_environment = 'production'
      AND metric_name IN ('bot.telemetry.dropped_spans', 'bot.telemetry.dropped_logs')
    GROUP BY metric_name, service_version, service_instance_id, process_pid, counter_epoch, aggregation_temporality
)
SELECT metric_name AS signal, SUM(dropped) AS dropped
FROM streams GROUP BY signal ORDER BY signal
